categories.name: Standard Procure-to-Pay
categories.description: Standard, high-frequency procurement paths where purchase orders are created, goods and invoice receipts are recorded, and invoices are cleared without significant delays or complications.
categories.rationale: These variants represent the backbone of normal operations (high frequency, moderate duration, clean linear progression ending in Clear Invoice).

categories.name: Quick Cancellation or Early Termination
categories.description: Short-lived variants featuring very low trace lengths and rapid execution times, typically resulting in purchase order deletion, basic creation, or initial goods receipt without full invoice processing.
categories.rationale: Distinctly short trace lengths and minimal durations characterize these early-stage or aborted procurements.

categories.name: Service Entry Sheet Processing
categories.description: Procurement paths focusing specifically on the recording of service entry sheets and goods receipts with minimal overhead or intermediate steps.
categories.rationale: These variants group around service-oriented activities (Record Service Entry Sheet) with very low durations.

categories.name: SRM System Transfer Failure
categories.description: Complex procurement variants originating in the SRM subsystem that suffer from transfer failures or communication issues with execution systems.
categories.rationale: Characterized by the presence of SRM lifecycle states and culminating explicitly in 'SRM: Transfer Failed (E.Sys.)'.

categories.name: Extreme Rework and Administrative Delay
categories.description: Extremely long-running variants characterized by massive trace lengths, repetitive loops of invoice creation, cancellations, payment block removals, and multi-year durations.
categories.rationale: These represent extreme outliers in terms of trace length (hundreds of activities), duration (years), and extensive rework observed across multiple steps.
